hindi: सोम तुम्हें आनन्दित करें; हे पत्थर के धारी, उदारता प्रदान करो; पवित्र वाणी (ब्रह्म) से द्वेष रखने वालों को मार गिराओ।
english: May the Somas gladden you; grant bounty, O wielder of the stone; strike down the haters of the sacred word (brahman).
notes: ut is read with mandantu (tmesis). brahman is taken as the sacred word or prayer; "priest" is an alternative.

hindi: हे स्तुतिप्रिय, हमारे निचोड़े हुए सोम को पियो; तुम मधु की धाराओं से अभिषिक्त किए जाते हो। हे इन्द्र, यश तुम्हारा ही दिया हुआ है।
english: O lover of praise, drink our pressed Soma; you are anointed with streams of honey. O Indra, glory is indeed given by you.
notes: tvādātam is read as tvā-dātam "given by you", with yaśaḥ as its subject; the second line is elliptical (no verb) and this construction is uncertain.

hindi: सदा इन्द्र तुम्हें अपनी ओर खींचे; और अब वह समीप आकर सम्मान करे। चुना हुआ देव नहीं, शूर तो इन्द्र है।
english: Always may Indra draw you hither, and now may he come near and honour you. Not a chosen god: the hero is Indra.
notes: Hard verse; carkṛṣat (intensive of √kṛṣ), saparyan, the case of vaḥ and the construction of the second line (na devo vṛtaḥ) are all uncertain, so the translation is tentative.

hindi: जैसे नदियाँ समुद्र में प्रवेश करती हैं, वैसे ही सोम की बूँदें तुममें प्रवेश करें। हे इन्द्र, तुमसे बढ़कर कोई नहीं है।
english: May the drops enter you as rivers enter the ocean. O Indra, nothing surpasses you.
notes: ati ricyate is taken as "surpasses" (with tvām as the standard of comparison); literally "is left over beyond you".

hindi: गाथा गाने वालों ने इन्द्र की स्तुति की; अर्क गाने वालों ने अर्क-मन्त्रों से बृहत् गान के साथ इन्द्र की स्तुति की; वाणियों ने इन्द्र की स्तुति की।
english: The singers of gāthā songs praised Indra; the chanters praised Indra with hymns (arka), loudly (or with the Bṛhat chant); the voices praised Indra.
notes: anūṣata governs all three clauses. bṛhat is either adverbial "loudly" or the name of the chant Bṛhat; both are possible.

hindi: इन्द्र हमें पोषण के लिए धन दें, जो ऋभुक्षण के समान और ऋभु के समान कुशल है; बलवान बलवान को दे।
english: May Indra give us, for refreshment, wealth that is mighty and skilful (ṛbhukṣan, ṛbhu); may the strong one give the strong.
notes: ṛbhukṣaṇam and ṛbhum are obscure here (adjectives of rayim, "Ṛbhu-like"). The object of the last clause (vājinam) is uncertain: "the strong one" or "strong (wealth)". The line ends without a stated receiver. The token "ṛbhu~" carries a tilde standing for anusvāra (ṛbhuṃ).

hindi: इन्द्र ने ही बड़े भय को परास्त कर दूर हटा दिया; क्योंकि वह दृढ़ और सब कुछ देखने वाला है।
english: Indra indeed, overcoming it, has driven the great fear away; for he is firm and all-surveying.
notes: abhī ṣad is obscure (abhi plus ṣat, perhaps "overcoming"); the analysis is tentative. vicarṣaṇi is taken as "all-surveying, all-seeing"; "active" is also possible.

hindi: हे स्तुतिप्रिय, ये स्तुतियाँ हर सोम-निचोड़ने पर तुम्हारे पास पहुँचती हैं, जैसे दूध देने वाली गायें बछड़े के पास।
english: O lover of praise, these songs approach you at every pressing, like milch cows to the calf.

hindi: अब हम इन्द्र और पूषन् को मित्रता के लिए, कल्याण के लिए, वाज की प्राप्ति के लिए पुकारें।
english: Now may we call upon Indra and Pūṣan, for friendship, for well-being, for winning the prize.
notes: indrā ... pūṣaṇā are dual forms of the pair "Indra and Pūṣan". The ~ in vaya~ stands for anusvāra.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुमसे ऊपर कोई नहीं, और तुमसे बड़ा कोई नहीं है, हे वृत्रहन्; तुम जैसा कोई नहीं है।
english: O Indra, no one is higher than you, nor is anyone greater, O slayer of Vṛtra; no one is thus as you are.
notes: "ki" and "kyevam" stand for kiḥ (na kiḥ, "no one"); the expected sandhi would be "na kir indra", so the printed form reflects the Sāmaveda text. uttaram is neuter in form (adverbial "beyond") where a masculine uttaraḥ would be expected.

hindi: तुम्हारे जनों के उद्धारक को, गायों से भरे वाज के दाता को, मैं एक साथ आगे बढ़कर स्तुति करूँ।
english: The saviour of your peoples, the bestower of the prize rich in cows, him I would praise forth alike.
notes: tradam is obscure (perhaps "protector" or "bestower"); samānam u pra is unclear (samānam "alike/together"). The object of the praise, presumably Indra, is not named in the unit; vaḥ "your" is plural and the sense is tentative.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुम्हारी स्तुतियाँ छोड़ी गई हैं; वे एक मन होकर तुम्हारी ओर उठ गई हैं, तुम वृषभ और स्वामी की ओर।
english: O Indra, your songs have been sent forth; of one accord they have risen toward you, the bull, the lord.
notes: ud ahāsata is taken as ud-√hā "rise up, go up".

hindi: वही मनुष्य अच्छी अगुवाई वाला है जिसकी रक्षा मरुद्गण, अर्यमा और द्रोहरहित मित्र करते हैं।
english: That mortal is indeed well-led whom the Maruts, whom Aryaman, the friends free from hostility, protect.
notes: mitrāḥ is plural (so not the god Mitra by himself): "friends" or "the Mitras". The tokens gha and the pairing of Maruts and Aryaman are as printed.

hindi: जो वसु इच्छा करने योग्य है और जो दृढ़ स्थान में, स्थिर स्थान में, पर्शान में छिपाकर ले जाया गया है, हे इन्द्र, उसे यहाँ ले आओ।
english: The desirable wealth that has been carried away, in the firm place, in the steady place, in the parśāna, bring that here, O Indra.
notes: vīḍau, sthire and parśāne are locatives of obscure sense (parśāne is not translated); whether the "firm/steady" ones are places or persons is uncertain. The wealth is the object of bhara through tat.

hindi: तुम्हारे जनों के प्रसिद्ध, वृत्र को सबसे अच्छी तरह मारने वाले दल को मैं बड़ी उदारता के लिए आगे बढ़कर पुकारता हूँ।
english: I invoke forth your famed host of the peoples, the best slayer of Vṛtra, for great bounty.
notes: Uncertain construction. āśiṣe is read here as ā + śiṣe (1 sg. of √śās, "I direct, invoke"); the alternative is a dative noun āśiṣe "for the prayer/blessing". The syntax of the first line (an accusative śardham with pra) is also unclear.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हम तुम्हारी कीर्ति के लिए उपयुक्त रूप से पहुँचें, हे शूर, तुम जैसे के लिए; हे शक्र, परेमणि में भी उपयुक्त रूप से।
english: Fitly may we attain to your fame, O Indra, O hero, as men of one like you; fitly, O mighty one, in the paremaṇi.
notes: ta in "araṃ ta indra" is te before a vowel (te indra gives ta indra). paremaṇi is obscure (a locative, perhaps "in the going beyond"); tvāvataḥ is a genitive whose connection is unclear. The sense is tentative.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, प्रातःकाल हमारे उस सोम को ग्रहण करो जो भुने अन्न, दलिया, पूओं और स्तुति-पाठ के साथ है।
english: O Indra, in the morning enjoy ours, accompanied by roasted grain, porridge, cakes and recitation.
notes: The accusative adjectives in line 1 agree with an unexpressed object (the offering, presumably the Soma); naḥ is read as "our (offering)", but "us" is also possible.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, तुमने जल के झाग से नमुचि का सिर उतार दिया, जब तुमने सब प्रतिद्वन्द्वियों को जीत लिया।
english: O Indra, with the foam of the waters you twisted off the head of Namuci, when you conquered all rivals.
notes: Namuci is a name; the story is not supplied. ajaya for ajayaḥ before spṛdhaḥ: the printed form drops the visarga.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, ये तुम्हारे सोम हैं, जो निचोड़े जा चुके हैं और जो अभी निचोड़े जाने हैं; हे प्रचुर धन वाले, इनसे आनन्दित हो।
english: These Somas are yours, O Indra, those pressed and those still to be pressed; rejoice in them, O abounding in wealth.
notes: sotvāḥ is read as "to be pressed" (future sense) contrasting with sutāsaḥ; the exact form is uncertain. ta is te before a vowel. prabhū-vasu: "abounding in wealth"; "wealth-lord" is also possible.

hindi: तुम्हारे लिए सोम निचोड़े गए हैं और कुशा बिछाई गई है, हे तेजस्वी; हे इन्द्र, स्तुति करने वालों पर कृपा करो।
english: For you the Somas are pressed and the sacred grass is spread, O radiant one; O Indra, be gracious to the singers.

words.gram: m. nom. pl. pres. part. denom. √vājaya

hindi: तुम सब, वाज की इच्छा करने वाले, सौ शक्तियों वाले, सबसे उदार इन्द्र में बूँदों से सींचो, जैसे कृवि में।
english: Pour in, with the drops, into Indra, the hundred-powered, the most bountiful, as into a kṛvi, you who seek the prize.

text_flags.why: possible: ā ... siñca needs an accusative object, as with the accusatives śatakratum and maṃhiṣṭhaṃ; the parallel in the Ṛgveda has indraṃ

notes: The word kṛvi is obscure (a vessel, well or similar). The plural vājayantaḥ with singular siñca is as printed.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, यहाँ से भी हमारे पास आओ, सौ वाज दिलाने वाली शक्ति से, हज़ार वाज दिलाने वाली शक्ति से।
english: From here also, O Indra, come to us with a refreshment that wins a hundred prizes, that wins a thousand prizes.
notes: iṣā is read as "refreshment, nourishment"; "strength" is also possible.

hindi: वृत्र को मारने वाले ने जन्म लेते ही बाण उठा लिया और माता से पूछा, "कौन उग्र हैं? कौन प्रसिद्ध हैं?"
english: As soon as he was born, the slayer of Vṛtra took up the arrow and asked his mother: "Who are the mighty ones? Who indeed are famed?"
notes: vṛtrahā is read as a subject epithet; the person is not named in the unit (Indra by context only). The verb pṛcchat with vi is taken as "asked"; the lines are read as a question put to the mother.

hindi: हम सहायता के लिए बृबदुक्थ को, सरकती (उदार) भुजा वाले को पुकारते हैं; जो सिद्ध करता और कार्य करता है, सहायता के लिए।
english: We call Bṛbaduktha, of the gliding arm, for help: the one who accomplishes and acts, for aid.
notes: Obscure on several points: bṛbaduktha (a name or the epithet "of great hymns", possibly spelling for bṛhaduktha), the compound sṛpra-karasna, and the form sādhaḥ in line 2, which does not parse as a clear verb or noun; its link to kṛṇvantam is a guess.

hindi: सीधे मार्गदर्शन से वरुण, मित्र, जो ज्ञानी है, हमें ले चलता है; अर्यमा देवों के साथ एकमत होकर।
english: By straight guidance Varuṇa and Mitra, the wise, lead us; Aryaman, in accord with the gods.
notes: nayati is a singular indicative; the Ṛgveda parallel is thought to have the imperative nayatu ("may he lead"). The verb is singular though several subjects are listed. vidvān is singular and may qualify one of the subjects; the translation treats the gods as one group.

hindi: जैसे दूर से भी यहीं हो, जब उस विद्यमान लाल रूप वाले ने चमक बिखेरी, तो उसने अपनी किरण को सब प्रकार से फैला दिया।
english: As if from afar yet here, when the ruddy-formed one who exists shone, he spread his light out in every way.
notes: Very uncertain. sataḥ (genitive of "being") and the identity of the subject (aruṇapsuḥ, ruddy-formed) are unclear; the first line may be read differently.

hindi: हे मित्र और वरुण, हमारे लिए चरागाह को घी से सींचो, और लोकों को मधुरता से, हे सुकर्मा।
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our pasture-land with ghee, and the regions with sweetness, O highly skilled ones.
notes: ghṛta is rendered "ghee"; it can also mean "melted fat, fluid". sukratū: "of good will or skill".

hindi: उन पुत्रों ने यज्ञों में स्तुतियों को लक्ष्यों तक ऊपर फैलाया; रँभाती हुई, घुटने की ओर जाने के लिए।
english: Those sons stretched the songs up to the goals in the sacrifices; the bellowing ones, to go knee-ward.
notes: Obscure. The referents of sūnavaḥ and vāśrāḥ are not stated (the ud in udu is read with atnata); abhijñu "knee-ward" and the relation of line 2 to line 1 are uncertain; kāṣṭhā may be a singular.

hindi: विष्णु ने इस (जगत्) को पार किया, उसने अपना पद तीन प्रकार से रखा; वह उसके धूलभरे (पद) में समाया हुआ है।
english: Viṣṇu strode across this, and set down his step in three ways; it is gathered up in his dusty (step).
notes: The object idam is understood as "this (world)". pāṃsule is the printed form (a form of pāṃsula "dusty"; the Ṛgveda has pāṃsure). The line 2 subject "it" (the world) is not stated.

hindi: क्रोध से सोम निचोड़ने वाले को पार कर जाओ, और जिसने निचोड़ा है उसके पास पहुँचो; उसकी दी हुई वस्तु में निचोड़ा सोम पियो।
english: Pass beyond the one who presses in anger; drive up to the one who has pressed; in his gift drink the pressed Soma.
notes: manyuṣāviṇam is obscure (manyu "anger, ardour"; sāvin "pressing"); "pressing with ardour" is an alternative. The object of eraya is not stated (Indra is addressed implicitly).

hindi: महान्, अत्यन्त प्रज्ञावान देव के लिए कौन-सा वचन कहा जाता है? वही निश्चय उसकी वृद्धि करने वाला है।
english: What word is recited, then, for the great, very wise god? That, indeed, is his strengthening.
notes: The god is not named. śasyate could also be read as a dative participle "to the god who is praised".

words.gram: n. acc. sg. pres. part. pass. √śaṃs
n. acc. sg. pres. part. pass. √gai

hindi: पाठ किया जाता हुआ उक्थ, और ... यहाँ पाठ अस्पष्ट है ...; और न गाया जाता हुआ गायत्र।
english: The hymn being recited, and ... the text here is obscure ...; nor the gāyatra being sung.
notes: Obscure; no reliable reading. The splitting nāgo = na + āgaḥ and the sense of rayirā ciketa ("wealth has noticed") are guesses. The two halves are parallel (recited hymn, sung gāyatra) but the verb and negation structure are unclear. Do not rely on this translation.

hindi: इन्द्र स्तुतियों से सबसे अधिक आनन्द देने वाला है और वाजों का स्वामी है; वह हरे घोड़ों वाला, निचोड़े हुए सोमों का मित्र है।
english: Indra, most gladdening through hymns and lord of prizes, the owner of bay horses, the friend of the pressed Somas.
notes: mandiṣṭha can be passive ("most gladdened") as well as "most gladdening". No finite verb: the unit is a nominal description of Indra.

hindi: हमारे निचोड़े हुए सोम के पास अपने बलों के साथ आओ; क्रोध मत करो, जैसे युवा पत्नी वाला कोई बड़ा पुरुष।
english: Come up to our pressed Soma with your strengths; do not be angry, like a great man with a young wife.
notes: The simile (mahāñ iva yuvajāniḥ) is idiomatic and its point is uncertain; "do not be angry/displeased" is the plain sense of mā hṛṇīthāḥ.

hindi: हे वसु, कब स्तुति ... यहाँ पाठ अस्पष्ट है ...; लम्बा निचोड़ा हुआ सोम वातापि के लिए।
english: When, O good one, the praise ... the text here is obscure ...; the long pressed Soma for Vātāpya.
notes: Obscure and possibly corrupt: ā ava śmaśā rudhadvāḥ cannot be analysed reliably, and vātāpyāya (a name or an epithet) is uncertain. The translation gives only the parts that can be read.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, ब्राह्मण के दान से ऋतु-ऋतु के अनुसार सोम पियो; तुम्हारी यह मित्रता अटूट है।
english: O Indra, from the bounty of the priest, drink Soma season by season; this friendship of yours is unbroken.
notes: The token "ranu" begins with the r of ṛtūṃr (ṛtūn before anu); the previous token somamṛtū~ ends in the tilde standing for anusvāra. The words brāhmaṇāt rādhasaḥ may mean "from the Brāhmaṇa-priest's bounty" (the exact construction is uncertain).

hindi: हे इन्द्र, हे स्तुतिप्रिय, हम तो तुम्हारे ही स्तोता हैं; हे सोमपायी, तुम हमें उत्साहित करो।
english: O Indra, O lover of praise, we are indeed your praisers; O Soma-drinker, quicken us.

hindi: हे इन्द्र, किसी भी संग्राम में हमारे शरीरों में पौरुष स्थापित करो; हे सदा विजयी, हे उग्र, मर्दाना बल भी।
english: O Indra, in whatever contests, place manliness in our bodies; O ever-victorious, O mighty one, give manly strength.
notes: pṛkṣu is taken as "in contests/battles". pauṃsyam is a second object of dhehi; the verb is repeated in the translation. The tilde in pau~syam stands for anusvāra.

hindi: इस प्रकार ही तुम वीरों को चाहने वाले हो, इस प्रकार शूर और दृढ़; इस प्रकार तुम्हारा मन प्रसन्न किए जाने योग्य है।
english: Thus indeed you are a lover of heroes, thus a hero and firm; thus your mind can be won.
notes: vīrayu: "desiring heroes" (alternatively "heroic"). rādhyam manaḥ is taken as "a mind that can be won over (propitiated)".

hindi: हे शूर, हम तुम्हारे सामने ऊँचे स्वर में स्तुति करते हैं, जैसे न दुही हुई गायें रँभाती हैं; इस चलते जगत् के स्वामी को, सूर्य का प्रकाश देखने वाले को, हे इन्द्र, स्थिर रहने वाले के स्वामी को।
english: O hero, we roar to you like unmilked milch cows; to you, the ruler of this moving world, the seer of the light of heaven, the ruler, O Indra, of what stands still.
notes: The second line is longer than a normal half-verse (it carries two pādas of the source verse); the unit grouping follows the edition. tasthuṣaḥ is genitive of the participle "of what is standing (still)".

hindi: हम स्तोता तुम्हें ही वाज की प्राप्ति में पुकारते हैं; मनुष्य तुम्हें, हे इन्द्र, वृत्र-संग्रामों में सज्जनों के स्वामी के रूप में, और घोड़े की दौड़ों में तुम्हें पुकारते हैं।
english: We singers call on you indeed in the winning of the prize; men call on you, O Indra, lord of the good, in the Vṛtra-battles, and on you in the races of the steed.

text_flags.why: possible: the printed form drops a syllable; the expected nominative plural is kāravaḥ (also the metre of 8 syllables)

notes: havāmahe is understood again in line 2 ("men call on you"). vṛtreṣu is taken as "in the battles against Vṛtra (obstructors)".

hindi: जैसा मैं जानता हूँ, वैसे अच्छे दान वाले इन्द्र की ओर तुम आगे बढ़कर स्तुति करो; जो धनी और उदार इन्द्र स्तोताओं को मानो हज़ारों से देता है।
english: Sing forth to Indra, rich in bounty, as I know how; he who, bountiful and rich in wealth, gives to the singers as if by thousands.
notes: vaḥ ("for you") is plural while arca is singular; yathā vide could also be "as it is known". śikṣati: "gives, assists".

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. mid. √mad

hindi: उस अद्भुत, शत्रुओं को हराने वाले, सोम-रस और धन से आनन्दित होने वाले इन्द्र को हम गीतों से पुकारते हैं, जैसे दूध देने वाली गायें बाड़ों में बछड़े की ओर।
english: Him, the wondrous, the overcomer of assailants, rejoicing in the Soma-juice and the wealth, we roar to Indra with songs, like milch cows to the calf in the stalls.
notes: vasoḥ is genitive of vasu ("wealth" or "the good one") and its link with mandānam is uncertain. The object tam is Indra, named only in line 2.

hindi: तुम्हारे लिए वेग से, पीड़ित होकर, हम सहायता के लिए धन ढूँढने वाले इन्द्र को पुकारते हैं; जहाँ सोम निचोड़ा जाता है उस यज्ञ में ऊँचे स्वर से गाते हुए, मैं पुकारता हूँ, जैसे बोझ के लिए कर्मी को।
english: With speed, hard-pressed, we call on Indra, the finder of wealth, for help; singing loudly at the rite where Soma is pressed, I call, as one calls a worker to the burden.
notes: Obscure in places: tarobhiḥ vaḥ, sabādhaḥ, and the comparison huve bharaṃ na kāriṇam (bharam "burden, fray") are uncertain. The ~ in indra~ stands for anusvāra.

hindi: वेगवान ही सहयोगी और प्रचुर बुद्धि के साथ वाज जीतना चाहता है। तुम्हारे लिए मैं बहुत पुकारे गए इन्द्र को गीत से अपनी ओर झुकाता हूँ, जैसे बढ़ई अच्छी लकड़ी के पहिए की परिधि को।
english: The swift one wishes to win the prize with abundant inspiration and an ally. For you I bend hither Indra, the much-invoked, with song, as a carpenter bends the rim of good wood.
notes: puraṃdhyā: "with abundant gifts/inspiration" (puraṃdhi is wide-ranging). The subject of line 1 (taraṇiḥ, "the swift one") is not identified. The simile is read with nemiṃ as the rim of a wheel.

words.gloss: mixed with milk, rich in cows

hindi: हे इन्द्र, निचोड़े हुए, रसीले, दूध मिले सोम को पियो और हमारे लिए आनन्दित हो; भोज में हमारे बन्धु बनो, वृद्धि के लिए; तुम्हारी बुद्धियाँ हमारी रक्षा करें।
english: O Indra, drink of the pressed, juicy, milk-rich Soma and be gladdened for us; be our kinsman at the feast, for growth; may your thoughts help us.
notes: The pluta 3 after vṛdhe is a chant mark and is not translated; the following asmān has lost its initial a (avagraha) after the prolonged e. gomataḥ: "rich in cows/milk" with sutasya rasinaḥ. bodhi: "be mindful, be our friend".

hindi: तुम ही आओ, चेरु के लिए; धन पाने के लिए भाग पाओ; हे मघवन्, गायों की खोज के लिए बरसाओ; हे इन्द्र, इच्छा-पूर्ति के लिए घोड़ा भी बरसाओ।
english: You indeed, come to the cera; find a share for the gaining of wealth; pour forth, O Maghavan, for the quest of cattle; pour forth, O Indra, a horse for the wish.
notes: Obscure: cerave (a dative of unclear meaning), vasuttaye (taken as a form for "winning wealth") and the exact sense of the second ud are uncertain. The tilde in tva~ stands for anusvāra.

hindi: तुम में से अन्तिम की भी वसिष्ठ उपेक्षा नहीं करता; हे मरुतो, आज हमारे सोम-निचोड़ने पर सभी इच्छा रखने वाले साथ मिलकर पिएँ।
english: Vasiṣṭha does not slight any of you, not even the last; O Maruts, today at our pressing let all of you who desire it drink together.

text_flags.why: possible: "not even the last" reads better with cana than with ca na ("and not")

notes: parimaṃste is uncertain (taken as "slights, disregards"). vasiṣṭha is read as the name (the sage); it may also be the superlative "wealthiest". The shift from the vocative marutaḥ to the third-person imperative is as printed.

hindi: हे मित्रो, किसी और की स्तुति मत करो और हानि मत उठाओ; सोम निचोड़ने पर मिलकर केवल वृषभ इन्द्र की स्तुति करो और बार-बार उक्थों का पाठ करो।
english: Friends, do not recite anything else, and do not harm yourselves; together at the pressing praise only Indra, the bull, and recite the hymns again and again.
notes: mā riṣaṇyata: "do not do harm" or "do not come to harm"; the second is used. The tildes in śa~sata stand for anusvāra.
